note: Original classroom practice. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish systematically recording transactions from related business activities.
questions.prompt: A shoe repairer takes bookings, fixes shoes and records each customer payment with its date and amount. Which activity is book-keeping? Explain what makes that activity book-keeping.
questions.answer: Recording each payment with its date and amount is book-keeping because it creates an organised record of financial transactions.
questions.explanation: Bookings and repairs help run the business. The payment record tracks money received.

markingGuide.description: Identifies recording customer payments.
Explains the systematic recording of financial transactions.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain how transaction records help a business account for its spending.
questions.prompt: At month-end, a school cooperative treasurer remembers paying for tape and labels but cannot recall which cost more. Describe the entries that would answer the question and give a reason to record them on the day of purchase.
questions.answer: Record the date, item and amount for each purchase. The amounts can then be compared. Recording promptly reduces the chance of forgetting which amount belongs to which item.
questions.explanation: Records let another reader trace the amounts to the purchases after the details are forgotten.

markingGuide.description: Identifies entries that link purchases to amounts.
Explains a benefit of prompt recording.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain why integrity is important in book-keeping.
questions.prompt: After a market day, the cash counted is less than the balance shown in the records. A friend tells the book-keeper to enter an expense without evidence so the figures agree. What should the book-keeper do, and what quality does that show?
questions.answer: Keep the existing record, report the difference and check receipts and entries for its cause. Refusing to invent an expense shows integrity.
questions.explanation: An invented expense would conceal the difference and make the records unreliable.

markingGuide.description: Proposes reporting or investigating the actual difference without inventing an expense.
Identifies honesty or integrity and connects it to the decision.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply discretion when responding to an unauthorised request for financial records.
questions.prompt: While the treasurer is away, a visitor asks a pupil to share a file listing payments and names of club members. The visitor gives no reason and has no permission. What should the pupil do, and why is this a useful quality in a book-keeper?
questions.answer: Keep the file private and direct the visitor to the treasurer or other authorised person. This shows discretion and protects members’ payment information.
questions.explanation: Accurate records can contain private information. Access should follow the club’s authorisation process.

markingGuide.description: Keeps the records private or refers the request to an authorised person.
Explains how discretion protects the recorded information.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.subtopic: Checking a posting against its evidence
questions.learningObjective: Use a source amount to identify and correct a transcription error.
questions.prompt: A cloth seller’s payment voucher and cash count both support an expense of ₦1,640. A helper entered ₦1,460. By how much was the expense understated? Give one way to correct the record while keeping a trace of what changed.
questions.answer: It was understated by ₦180. Correct the entry to ₦1,640 and retain a dated note linking the change to the voucher and identifying who corrected it.
questions.explanation: Subtract ₦1,460 from ₦1,640. An identifiable correction lets a later reader explain the changed figure.

markingGuide.description: Finds an understatement of ₦180.
Proposes a correction traceable to the original entry and its evidence.

verification.purpose: Check the understatement in the expense record.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Select a digital tool to meet an everyday book-keeping need.
questions.prompt: A snack stall keeps daily transactions as separate photos of notebook pages. The owner wants to find all recorded payments to a single supplier within a chosen month. Suggest a suitable digital tool and say how the owner should organise the information in it.
questions.answer: Use a spreadsheet with a row per transaction and columns for date, supplier, amount and document reference. Filter the rows by supplier and date.
questions.explanation: Structured fields can be filtered directly. Document references help the owner check the results against the evidence.

markingGuide.description: Chooses a suitable tool, such as a spreadsheet or book-keeping application.
Explains a viable way to find the specified transactions using searchable fields.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Identify an original transaction document and distinguish it from a later report.
questions.prompt: A club sells used books at a fair. Its treasurer has a sale receipt for each buyer and a sheet made a week later showing the total raised. Which of these records is a source document for one buyer’s payment? Explain.
questions.answer: The receipt for that buyer is the source document because it records evidence of the individual payment. The total sheet summarises many payments.
questions.explanation: A source document is evidence from which an individual transaction can be recorded or checked.

markingGuide.description: Selects the receipt for that buyer.
Explains that it evidences the individual transaction.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Choose relevant evidence to check a report that a supplier has already been paid.
questions.prompt: A vendor’s invoice lists school aprons and an amount due. A staff member points to that invoice as evidence that the amount was paid. Explain what the invoice establishes and name a document that could support the payment claim.
questions.answer: The invoice shows the vendor’s charge. A receipt issued by the vendor for that invoice could acknowledge payment.
questions.explanation: An amount billed and an amount paid are different facts. The payment record should be traceable to the charge.

markingGuide.description: Explains that the invoice establishes the amount billed.
Names suitable linked payment evidence, such as a supplier receipt.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Classify one invoice from the perspectives of seller and buyer.
questions.prompt: A bag maker sends invoice BM-14 to a stationery shop for goods supplied on credit. How should each business describe BM-14 in its records? Explain why the invoice number can be the same on both copies.
questions.answer: It is a sales invoice for the bag maker and a purchase invoice for the stationery shop. Both copies concern the same transaction and can carry the supplier’s invoice reference BM-14.
questions.explanation: The description reflects the business’s role in the transaction. A shared reference helps match the two copies.

markingGuide.description: Correctly classifies the invoice for both parties.
Explains the shared transaction reference.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Use line quantities and prices on a till tape to check a sale total.
questions.prompt: A cash register tape has two lines: 3 folders at ₦280 each and 1 marker at ₦410. The total on the tape is ₦1,150. Assume no discounts or other charges. Show the expected total and state what should be checked before recording the sale.
questions.answer: The folders cost ₦840 and the marker costs ₦410, so the expected total is ₦1,250. Check which quantities, prices and total the till actually recorded before relying on the tape.
questions.explanation: Multiply the folder quantity by its unit price and add the marker price. The resulting total differs from the tape by ₦100.

markingGuide.description: Shows the correct folder line amount and expected total.
Identifies the discrepancy and proposes checking the recorded details.

verification.purpose: Verify the size of the discrepancy.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain the effect of a seller-issued credit note against an unpaid invoice.
questions.prompt: A supplier bills a shop ₦9,400. Before payment, the supplier accepts a damaged item back and issues a credit note for ₦1,700 against that bill. State the remaining amount due and explain why the shop should keep the credit note with the invoice.
questions.answer: The remaining amount due is ₦7,700. Keeping the credit note with the invoice shows why less is due than the original bill states.
questions.explanation: The seller’s credit note reduces the amount payable against the invoice.

markingGuide.description: Calculates the remaining amount due as ₦7,700.
Explains the documented reduction and the link to the invoice.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Interpret an agreed seller-issued debit note that increases an invoice amount.
questions.prompt: A seller and buyer agree that an unpaid invoice omitted a ₦650 delivery charge. The seller issues a debit note for that charge and quotes the original invoice number. Explain the effect on the buyer’s amount due and why the reference matters.
questions.answer: The buyer owes ₦650 more. The original invoice number identifies the bill to which the adjustment belongs.
questions.explanation: In this scenario the seller issues the note to document a mutually agreed increase in the amount due.

markingGuide.description: States the increase of ₦650.
Explains that the invoice reference links the adjustment to the original bill.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Identify cheque details and distinguish a payment instruction from confirmed settlement.
questions.prompt: A shop receives a cheque for a credit sale and makes a practice record of it. Name three details on the cheque that help identify the payment instruction. Explain why the shop might also check its bank record.
questions.answer: Record the cheque number, date and amount. The shop checks its bank record to confirm whether the cheque cleared and the amount was credited.
questions.explanation: Other useful identifying details include the drawer and payee. Recording a cheque received and confirming settlement are separate steps.

markingGuide.description: Names three valid identifying details.
Explains that the bank record can confirm clearance or credit.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.learningObjective: Create paper and digital versions of a receipt from a fictional payment brief.
questions.prompt: On 6 May 2026, the fictional Cedar School Shop received ₦2,300 cash from Nneka Obi as part-payment for order CS-17. Create a paper receipt and a matching typed version. Choose an identifying receipt number and show which order and payment the receipt covers.
questions.answer: Receipt R-021. Cedar School Shop received ₦2,300 cash from Nneka Obi on 6 May 2026 as part-payment for order CS-17. The paper and typed versions show the same information.
questions.explanation: The receipt acknowledges money actually received. The order reference identifies the transaction, and the receipt number distinguishes this acknowledgement from others.

markingGuide.description: Supplies both versions with a matching receipt identifier.
Shows the issuer, payer and date.
Records ₦2,300 cash and identifies it as part-payment for CS-17.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.subtopic: Preparing an invoice for a credit sale
questions.learningObjective: Create a simple sales invoice with traceable line items and an unpaid total.
questions.prompt: Prepare invoice SW-08 dated 14 May 2026 for Soma Weaving to send to Hill Craft Club. The club received 4 mats at ₦1,350 each and 2 baskets at ₦2,200 each on credit. Assume no taxes or other charges. Show the quantities, unit prices, line amounts and total due.
questions.answer: Invoice SW-08, 14 May 2026, from Soma Weaving to Hill Craft Club. Mats: 4 × ₦1,350 = ₦5,400. Baskets: 2 × ₦2,200 = ₦4,400. Total due: ₦9,800.
questions.explanation: Each line amount is the quantity multiplied by its unit price. The two amounts sum to the amount billed.

markingGuide.description: Shows the invoice identifier, date, seller and buyer.
Shows both correct quantities, unit prices and line amounts.
Shows ₦9,800 as the total due.
